answer: Attackers pool what clones earn, so give each identity a sinkhole: a unique, well-paid but unverifiable micro-job, one marked with an umber seal, another with an opal code, each with different hidden terms. Only its assigned identity should ever act on it or quote it. A pooled operator leaks: one clone redeems a sibling bait, another repeats hidden terms in its own work, and the set resolves, like stars from a nebula, into one cluster. Honest agents never saw other sinkholes, so they cannot cross them; farms sharing one stream cross-contaminate and expose themselves.
